skill.name: cold-offer
skill.description: Draft a cold outreach offer with a concrete finding, a small solution sample, and a first email without a paid product pitch.
skill.summary: Create finding-led outreach drafts and check their structure with a local Python validator.
skill.author: cmj-hub

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are harmless documentation, CSS, encoding markers, or legitimate local tooling. Confirmed risks affect optional asset renderers: unsafe HTML insertion, inline script serialization, CSS interpolation, and unconditional frame directory deletion. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious exfiltration; the Python scorer performs local validation without network access.

remediation.issue: The demo renderer inserts response and artifact text through innerHTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Build elements with DOM APIs and assign supplied text with textContent; add tests containing HTML tags and event handlers.

remediation.issue: JSON serialization does not prevent supplied text from closing the demo page script element.
remediation.suggestion: Escape less-than characters in serialized data before embedding it, or load data through a separate non-executable resource.

remediation.issue: Both renderers interpolate accent_color directly into a style element.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only valid hexadecimal colors before interpolation; reject other values and test style element termination attempts.

remediation.issue: The demo renderer recursively deletes the output-derived frames directory before verifying ownership.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique temporary directory and clean up only that directory in a finally block.

semantic_findings.title: Inline Script Breakout Through Specification Data
semantic_findings.description: The demo renderer embeds JSON.stringify output directly in a script element. Supplied strings containing a closing script tag can terminate it and inject executable markup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: JSON.stringify does not escape HTML script terminators. The browser parses these serialized values inside an executable script element before DOM insertion.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked Color Value Can Escape Style Elements
semantic_findings.description: Both renderers interpolate supplied accent_color values directly into style elements. A crafted value can close the style element and introduce scripts or external resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Neither renderer validates accent_color before HTML interpolation. Text escaping elsewhere does not protect this separate style-element context.

content.user_title: Draft Cold Offers Around Concrete Findings
content.value_statement: Cold outreach often asks for a purchase before showing useful work. This skill structures a finding, a small solution sample, and a first email with local draft checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide an offer draft with three parts: finding, prototype, and first email.
Structure a first email around a public-page observation and a small solution sample.
Check that the three required draft fields contain nonempty strings.
Reject first emails containing configured paid-product pitch phrases.
Validate local draft files or standard input using Python without network access.
Print accepted draft sections and return distinct success, rejection, and input-error exit codes.
limitations: The skill does not send emails, book meetings, or manage outreach campaigns.
The scorer matches fixed phrases; it cannot reliably determine sales intent or overall writing quality.
The workflow does not independently verify findings, build a working solution, or guarantee recipient responses.
Optional asset renderers require extra tools, request external fonts, and have unresolved injection and filesystem risks.

use_cases.title: Founder Outreach
use_cases.description: Draft a first email that shares a specific public-page observation and a small sample instead of requesting a demo.

use_cases.title: Consulting Offer Preparation
use_cases.description: Package a verified business finding with a limited solution sample before discussing a larger paid engagement.

use_cases.title: Team Draft Review
use_cases.description: Check draft completeness and configured pitch phrases before a human reviews the message for sending.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a First Offer
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a cold offer from this verified observation: [finding]. Include a finding, a small solution sample, and a first email without a product pitch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a structured draft from an existing observation.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a Pitch
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this email: [draft]. Lead with [verified finding], name [prepared sample], and remove purchase requests, meeting requests, and demo invitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: revise an existing sales message.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my draft at [local path]. Use the local scorer to check required fields and pitch phrases, then suggest revisions without sending anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: check a saved draft using the supplied validator.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare and Review Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three offer variants from [verified finding] and [prepared sample]. Compare clarity, validate each locally, and explain limitations of the phrase checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare alternative drafts with human judgment and local validation.

output_examples.input: Draft an offer about a homepage requesting meetings before showing any work.
output: Finding: Your homepage asks for a meeting before showing a work sample.

First email: Your homepage asks for a meeting before showing any work. I prepared a one-page alternative. May I share the full report?

output_examples.input: Check a complete draft whose first email says: Buy our retainer.
output: Result: Rejected because the first email contains a configured paid-product pitch phrase.
Revision: Share the specific finding and the prepared sample instead of asking for a purchase.

output_examples.input: Check a draft with a finding and first email but no prototype.
output: Revision: Add a nonempty prototype description before checking again.

best_practices: Use verified public observations and describe only samples you have actually prepared.
Review scorer results manually because fixed phrase checks can reject harmless text or miss sales pitches.
Keep the core drafting workflow separate from optional asset renderers until their security issues are fixed.
anti_patterns: Inventing recipient problems or claiming unfinished work is already available.
Treating a successful scorer result as proof of accuracy, compliance, or effective outreach.
Passing untrusted specifications to the optional renderers or reusing directories containing important files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running the local scorer requires Python 3.

faq.question: Does the skill send the email?
faq.answer: No. It guides drafting and checks local input. You review and send the message through your own email tools.

faq.question: What does the leak section mean?
faq.answer: It means a concrete business issue observed on a public page or product. It does not mean private or stolen information.

faq.question: What does the scorer check?
faq.answer: It requires three nonempty text fields and rejects configured pitch phrases in the first email. It does not verify facts or assess writing quality.

faq.question: Does this require paid APIs or network access?
faq.answer: The Python scorer uses the standard library and no network. Optional asset renderers use browser tools, external fonts, and additional dependencies.

faq.question: Are the optional asset renderers safe for untrusted input?
faq.answer: No. They have HTML, script, and style injection risks. The GIF renderer also deletes an output-derived frame directory without checking ownership.
